2: The Gospel of Thomas is a collection of sayings and tells nothing of the birth. The stories of the infancy found under the name of Thomas belong to a different and later work, the Infancy Gospel of Thomas. It keeps one saying that touches on the mother of Jesus:

- [agree] Thomas 79. A woman calls blessed the womb that bore him. Jesus calls blessed those who hear the Father’s word and keep it. Days will come when people bless the womb that never bore. (Compare Luke 11:27-28.){{fn:Luke 11:27-28. Thomas says “the Father’s word” where Luke says “the word of God”, and it is read here as Luke has it (see the note on “Father” on the page of sayings set aside). Agrees with Qur’an 3:42-47, where Maryam is honoured, and with 19:30-31, where the child states what he was commanded.}}
Sayings that conflict with the Qur’an, and sayings that only repeat another, are listed with the reason for each on the page of sayings set aside.
8: ## From the Gospel of Thomas

The Gospel of Thomas keeps many sayings of the teacher. Each carries a colour mark: green agrees with the Qur’an as the measure, blue is beyond the measure (the Qur’an says nothing either way), gold is unclear. The note on each gives its canonical parallel and the Qur’anic verse, or the reason for the mark.

- [unclear] Thomas 4. An old man should ask a week-old child about the place of life. The first will be last, and all will become one.{{fn:A riddle about an old man and a small child. Its sense is not given and no reading settles it.}}
- [unclear] Thomas 7. A lion eaten by a man is blessed, because it becomes human. A man eaten by a lion is cursed.{{fn:The lion and the man. No parallel and no clear sense.}}

- [unclear] Thomas 8. The wise fisherman keeps one large fish and throws back all the small ones. Let those with ears hear.{{fn:The wise fisherman. A parable found only here; Matthew 13:47-48 has a net, but the point is different.}}

- [agree] Thomas 9. The sower’s seed falls on road, rock and thorns, and some on good soil, which yields sixty and a hundredfold. (Compare Mark 4:3-9.){{fn:Mark 4:3-9; Matthew 13:3-9; Luke 8:5-8. Qur’an 2:261 likens the reward of giving to a grain that grows seven ears, a hundred grains in each.}}

- [unclear] Thomas 10. Jesus has set fire to the world and is watching over it until it blazes.{{fn:Fire cast upon the world. The sense is uncertain; compare Luke 12:49, where the fire is a figure of judgment.}}

- [beyond] Thomas 16. Jesus has come to bring division, not peace: fire, sword and war, and households set father against son. (Compare Luke 12:51-53.){{fn:Parallel to Luke 12:51-53. It makes Jesus’ mission fire, sword and war, which the Qur’anic portrait does not (19:33).}}

- [agree] Thomas 20. The kingdom is like a mustard seed, the smallest of seeds, which grows into a plant sheltering birds. (Compare Mark 4:30-32.){{fn:Mark 4:30-32; Matthew 13:31-32; Luke 13:18-19. Qur’an 14:24-26 likens a good word to a good tree, firm in root and high in branch.}}

- [unclear] Thomas 21. Mary asks what the disciples are like. They are children in a field that is not theirs, who give it back. Be on guard like a householder against a thief, and let a wise person reap when the grain ripens.{{fn:A string of images: children in a field, the householder and the thief, the reaper. The parts do not join. The thief is kept as saying 103.}}
- [unclear] Thomas 23. Jesus will choose one in a thousand and two in ten thousand, and they will stand as one.{{fn:One in a thousand and two in ten thousand. Obscure.}}

- [beyond] Thomas 24. The disciples ask to be shown where Jesus is. Light is inside a person of light, who lights the whole world. Without that light there is only darkness.{{fn:Light within a person of light. It depends on Thomas’s doctrine of an inner light, for which the Qur’an gives no basis.}}

- [agree] Thomas 25. Love your brother as your own soul and protect him as the pupil of your eye.{{fn:No canonical parallel in this form; compare Leviticus 19:18 and Mark 12:31. Qur’an 49:10: the believers are brothers; 59:9 praises those who prefer others to themselves.}}

- [agree] Thomas 26. You see the speck in your brother’s eye and not the beam in your own. Remove the beam first. (Compare Matthew 7:3-5.){{fn:Matthew 7:3-5; Luke 6:41-42. Qur’an 2:44 rebukes those who bid others to righteousness and forget themselves.}}

- [beyond] Thomas 27. Unless you fast from the world you will not find the kingdom, and unless you keep the Sabbath as a Sabbath you will not see the Father.{{fn:“Fast as regards the world” and keep the Sabbath “as a Sabbath”. The first phrase is unclear. The Qur’an says the Sabbath was laid on those who differed over it (16:124).}}

- [beyond] Thomas 29. If flesh came from spirit it is a wonder, but if spirit came from flesh it is a wonder of wonders. He marvels that such wealth lives in such poverty.{{fn:Flesh and spirit, wealth and poverty. It rests on Thomas’s own doctrine of body and spirit.}}

- [agree] Thomas 31. No prophet is welcomed in his own village, and no doctor heals those who know him. (Compare Luke 4:24.){{fn:Mark 6:4; Matthew 13:57; Luke 4:24; John 4:44. The Qur’an records messengers rejected by their own people: 36:13-30; 2:87.}}
- [agree] Thomas 32. A city built on a high mountain and fortified cannot fall or be hidden. (Compare Matthew 5:14.){{fn:Matthew 5:14. Qur’an 2:143 calls the community a witness over the nations.}}

- [agree] Thomas 33. Preach from the housetops what you hear. No one hides a lamp under a bushel. It goes on a stand for all to see. (Compare Matthew 10:27; 5:15.){{fn:Matthew 5:15 and 10:27; Luke 8:16 and 12:3. Qur’an 5:67: convey what has been sent down to you.}}
- [agree] Thomas 34. If a blind man leads a blind man, both fall into a pit. (Compare Matthew 15:14.){{fn:Matthew 15:14; Luke 6:39. Qur’an 6:50: are the blind and the seeing equal?}}
- [agree] Thomas 35. No one can plunder a strong man’s house without first binding his hands. (Compare Mark 3:27.){{fn:Mark 3:27; Matthew 12:29. Qur’an 4:76: the plot of Satan was ever weak.}}

- [agree] Thomas 36. Do not worry from morning to evening, or from evening to morning, about what you will wear. (Compare Matthew 6:25.){{fn:Matthew 6:25; Luke 12:22. Qur’an 65:3: whoever puts trust in God, He is enough for him.}}

- [agree] Thomas 42. Jesus says only: be passers-by.{{fn:No canonical parallel. Qur’an 57:20 and 18:45 call the life of this world a passing enjoyment, and the tradition says the same: be in this world as a stranger or a traveller (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Book of Softening the Hearts).}}

- [agree] Thomas 45. Grapes do not come from thorns or figs from thistles. A good person brings out good and an evil one brings out evil from what fills the heart. (Compare Matthew 7:16; 12:33-35.){{fn:Matthew 7:16-18 and 12:33-35; Luke 6:43-45. Qur’an 14:24-26 sets the good word beside the evil word.}}

- [agree] Thomas 47. No one can ride two horses or draw two bows or serve two masters. Old wine does not go into new skins, nor new wine into old. (Compare Luke 16:13; 5:36-39.){{fn:Luke 16:13; Matthew 6:24; Mark 2:21-22. Qur’an 39:29 sets the servant of many masters beside the servant of one.}}
- [agree] Thomas 54. Blessed are the poor, for the kingdom of heaven is theirs. (Compare Luke 6:20.){{fn:Luke 6:20; Matthew 5:3. Qur’an 90:12-16 and 107:1-3 on feeding the poor.}}

- [agree] Thomas 57. The kingdom is like a man whose enemy sowed weeds among his wheat. He lets both grow until harvest, when the weeds are pulled and burned. (Compare Matthew 13:24-30.){{fn:Matthew 13:24-30. Thomas begins “the kingdom of the Father”; Matthew has “the kingdom of heaven”. Qur’an 22:17: God will decide between them on the Day of Resurrection.}}
- [unclear] Thomas 58. Blessed is the one who has suffered and found life.{{fn:Blessed is the one who has suffered and found life. No clear sense.}}

- [unclear] Thomas 59. Look to the living one while you are alive. After death you will look for him and not be able to find him.{{fn:Look to “the living one” while you are alive. The reference is obscure.}}

- [unclear] Thomas 60. Jesus sees a Samaritan carrying a lamb to Judea. The lamb will be eaten only once it is dead. The disciples must find a place of rest so they do not become a corpse and be eaten.{{fn:The Samaritan with the lamb, a riddle about a corpse that is eaten. No parallel.}}

- [agree] Thomas 62. Jesus tells his mysteries to those worthy of them. Do not let your left hand know what your right is doing. (Compare Matthew 6:3.){{fn:Matthew 6:3. Qur’an 2:271: to give in secret is better.}}

- [agree] Thomas 63. A rich man plans to invest and fill his barns so that he lacks nothing, and he dies that night. (Compare Luke 12:16-21.){{fn:Luke 12:16-21. Qur’an 18:32-44, the owner of the two gardens, and 57:20.}}
- [beyond] Thomas 67. Whoever knows everything but lacks himself lacks everything.{{fn:Knowing the All yet lacking oneself. It is Thomas’s doctrine of self-knowledge.}}

- [agree] Thomas 68. Blessed are you when you are hated and persecuted, and no place will be found where you were persecuted. (Compare Matthew 5:11.){{fn:Matthew 5:11; Luke 6:22. Qur’an 2:214 on the trials of those who came before.}}

- [beyond] Thomas 69. Blessed are those persecuted within themselves, who have truly come to know the Father. Blessed are the hungry, for the belly of the one in need will be filled.{{fn:Those “persecuted within themselves” know the Father. It is Thomas’s doctrine of inward knowledge.}}

- [beyond] Thomas 70. What you bring forth from yourselves will save you. What you do not bring forth will destroy you.{{fn:What you bring forth from yourselves will save you. The Qur’an makes salvation depend on faith and righteous deeds, by God’s mercy (103:3).}}
- [unclear] Thomas 74. Lord, many stand around the trough but there is nothing in the well.{{fn:The trough and the cistern. Obscure.}}

- [agree] Thomas 76. The kingdom is like a merchant who finds a pearl, sells his goods and buys it. Seek likewise the treasure that does not fail, which no moth devours. (Compare Matthew 13:45-46.){{fn:Matthew 13:45-46; Luke 12:33. Qur’an 57:20-21 sets the lasting reward against the passing life.}}
- [beyond] Thomas 81. Let the one who has grown rich be king, and the one who has power renounce it.{{fn:The rich should reign and the powerful renounce it. The sense is unclear.}}

- [beyond] Thomas 83. Images are visible to people but the light in them is hidden by the image of the Father’s light. He will be revealed and his image hidden by his light.{{fn:Images and the light of the Father. It belongs to Thomas’s doctrine of image and light.}}

- [beyond] Thomas 84. You rejoice when you see your likeness. When you see the images that existed before you, which neither die nor appear, you will bear a great deal.{{fn:Images that came into being before you. It belongs to Thomas’s doctrine of a heavenly twin.}}

- [agree] Thomas 86. Foxes have holes and birds have nests, but the son of man has nowhere to lay his head. (Compare Matthew 8:20.){{fn:Matthew 8:20; Luke 9:58. Qur’an 25:20: the messengers ate food and walked in the markets.}}

- [beyond] Thomas 87. Wretched is the body that depends on a body, and wretched the soul that depends on both.{{fn:Wretched is the body that depends on a body. It rests on Thomas’s contempt for the body.}}

- [unclear] Thomas 88. The angels and prophets will come and give you what is yours. You should give them what you have and ask when they will come for what is theirs.{{fn:The angels and prophets come and give you what is yours. Obscure.}}

- [agree] Thomas 89. Why wash the outside of the cup? The one who made the inside made the outside. (Compare Luke 11:39-40.){{fn:Luke 11:39-40; Matthew 23:25. Qur’an 2:177: righteousness is not in turning the face but in faith and deeds.}}

- [agree] Thomas 90. Come to me, for my yoke is easy and my lordship gentle, and you will find rest. (Compare Matthew 11:28-30.){{fn:Matthew 11:28-30. Qur’an 2:185: God intends ease for you; 3:50: ʿĪsā made lawful some of what had been forbidden.}}

- [agree] Thomas 92. Seek and you will find. What you asked before and I did not say, I now want to tell, but you do not ask. (Compare Matthew 7:7.){{fn:Matthew 7:7; Luke 11:9. Qur’an 2:186: “I am near; I answer the call of the caller.”}}
- [agree] Thomas 94. Whoever seeks will find, and to the one who knocks it will be opened. (Compare Matthew 7:8.){{fn:Matthew 7:8; Luke 11:10. Qur’an 40:60: “Call upon Me and I will answer you.”}}

- [agree] Thomas 95. If you have money, do not lend it at interest. Give it to those from whom you will not get it back. (Compare Luke 6:34-35.){{fn:Luke 6:34-35. Qur’an 2:275-276: God has forbidden interest and makes charity increase.}}

- [agree] Thomas 96. The kingdom is like a woman who hides a little leaven in dough and makes large loaves. (Compare Matthew 13:33.){{fn:Matthew 13:33; Luke 13:20-21. Thomas says “the kingdom of the Father”; see the note on “Father” on the page of sayings set aside.}}

- [unclear] Thomas 97. The kingdom is like a woman carrying a jar of meal. The handle breaks on the road and the meal spills out unnoticed. At home she finds the jar empty.{{fn:The jar of meal that empties on the road. No parallel.}}

- [unclear] Thomas 98. The kingdom is like a man who wants to kill a powerful man. He tests his strength by driving his sword into the wall, and then kills him.{{fn:The man who tests his sword on a wall and then kills a powerful man. No parallel, and the violence of the image is unexplained.}}

- [agree] Thomas 107. The kingdom is like a shepherd whose largest sheep strays. He leaves the ninety-nine to find it, and says he loves it more than the ninety-nine. (Compare Matthew 18:12-13.){{fn:Matthew 18:12-13; Luke 15:3-7. Qur’an 39:53: do not despair of the mercy of God.}}
- [beyond] Thomas 112. Woe to the flesh that depends on the soul, and woe to the soul that depends on the flesh.{{fn:Woe to the flesh that depends on the soul. It is Thomas’s dualism.}}
Sayings that conflict with the Qur’an, and sayings that only repeat another, are listed with the reason for each on the page of sayings set aside.
9: The Gospel of Thomas keeps sayings that stand beside the Qur’anic portrait of Yaḥyā and of the first helpers. Each saying carries a colour mark: green agrees with the Qur’an, blue is beyond the measure, gold is unclear.

- [beyond] Thomas 13. Asked whom he resembles, Peter answers a righteous angel and Matthew a wise philosopher. Thomas says he cannot say. Jesus tells Thomas three things he will not repeat, for the others would stone him.{{fn:Rests on secret teaching given to Thomas alone. The Qur’an records no hidden doctrine, and ʿĪsā brings clear proofs (3:49-50).}}

- [agree] Thomas 46. No one born of woman is greater than John the Baptist, yet whoever becomes a child will know the kingdom and surpass John. (Compare Matthew 11:11.){{fn:Matthew 11:11; Luke 7:28. Qur’an 3:39 and 19:12-15 honour Yaḥyā as noble, chaste and a prophet.}}

- [agree] Thomas 73. The harvest is large and the workers are few. Ask the Lord to send workers. (Compare Matthew 9:37-38.){{fn:Matthew 9:37-38; Luke 10:2. Qur’an 3:52 and 61:14, where ʿĪsā asks who will be God’s helpers.}}

- [agree] Thomas 78. Why did you go out to the desert, to see a reed shaken by the wind, or people in fine clothes like your rulers? They wear luxury and cannot know the truth. (Compare Matthew 11:7-8.){{fn:Matthew 11:7-8; Luke 7:24-25. Qur’an 19:12-15 honours Yaḥyā, and 18:28 warns against desiring the adornment of this life.}}

- [agree] Thomas 99. Told that his brothers and mother are outside, Jesus says those who do the Father’s will are his brothers and mother. (Compare Mark 3:31-35.){{fn:Mark 3:31-35, which reads “the will of God”. Thomas says “my father”; see the note on “Father” on the page of sayings set aside.}}
Sayings that conflict with the Qur’an, and sayings that only repeat another, are listed with the reason for each on the page of sayings set aside.
22: The Gospel of Thomas has no Jerusalem narrative, but it keeps sayings that belong to these days. Green agrees with the Qur’an, blue is beyond the measure.

- [agree] Thomas 39. The Pharisees and scribes have hidden the keys of knowledge and neither enter nor let others enter. Be as wise as serpents and as innocent as doves. (Compare Matthew 23:13; 10:16.){{fn:Matthew 23:13; Luke 11:52. Qur’an 2:75-79 and 3:78 on those who conceal and distort the Book.}}

- [agree] Thomas 40. A vine planted apart from the Father is unsound and will be uprooted and destroyed. (Compare Matthew 15:13.){{fn:Matthew 15:13, which reads “my heavenly Father”. Qur’an 14:26: the evil word is like a bad tree, uprooted.}}

- [agree] Thomas 65. A vineyard owner sends servants to collect his share from tenants, who beat them. He sends his son, whom they kill. (Compare Mark 12:1-9.){{fn:Mark 12:1-9; Matthew 21:33-41; Luke 20:9-16. The Qur’an records the killing of messengers (2:87; 3:21). It does not say that ʿĪsā was killed (4:157); the parable is read here of the people’s habit toward messengers.}}

- [agree] Thomas 66. Show me the stone the builders rejected: it is the cornerstone. (Compare Mark 12:10.){{fn:Mark 12:10; Psalm 118:22. Compare the tradition of the brick that completes the house of the prophets (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Book of Virtues).}}

- [beyond] Thomas 71. Jesus will destroy this house and no one will be able to rebuild it. (Compare Mark 14:58.){{fn:Mark 14:58 gives this as the testimony of false witnesses. Thomas makes it Jesus’ own and leaves out the rebuilding. The Qur’an has no Temple saying.}}

- [agree] Thomas 102. Woe to the Pharisees, who are like a dog sleeping in the oxen’s feed trough, neither eating nor letting the oxen eat.{{fn:Matthew 23:13; Luke 11:52. The image of the dog in the manger is an old Greek proverb. Qur’an 62:5 likens those who carry the Torah and do not act upon it to a donkey carrying books.}}

- [agree] Thomas 104. Asked to pray and fast, Jesus asks what sin he has committed. When the bridegroom leaves the bridal chamber, then let them fast and pray. (Compare Mark 2:18-20.){{fn:Mark 2:18-20; Matthew 9:14-15; Luke 5:33-35. Qur’an 2:183 prescribes fasting; the saying defers it rather than abolishing it.}}
Sayings that conflict with the Qur’an, and sayings that only repeat another, are listed with the reason for each on the page of sayings set aside.
24: The Gospel of Thomas keeps sayings on watching, on the end and on the kingdom. Green agrees with the Qur’an, blue is beyond the measure, gold is unclear.

- [beyond] Thomas 11. This heaven and the one above it will pass. The dead do not live. Those who were one became two, and the question is what they will do as two.{{fn:The heaven that passes away and the one that became two. It depends on Thomas’s own doctrine of an original unity.}}

- [unclear] Thomas 18. The end is where the beginning is. Blessed is the one who stands at the beginning and will not taste death.{{fn:The end is where the beginning is. It belongs to Thomas’s scheme of origin and return, and its sense is obscure.}}

- [beyond] Thomas 38. The disciples have long wanted to hear these words and have no one else to hear them from. A time will come when they look for Jesus and do not find him.{{fn:A time will come when the disciples look for Jesus and do not find him. No source confirms it; compare John 7:34.}}

- [agree] Thomas 103. Fortunate is the one who knows where the robbers will enter and can arm himself before they do. (Compare Matthew 24:43.){{fn:Matthew 24:43; Luke 12:39. Qur’an 7:187 and 31:34: the Hour comes suddenly and its knowledge is with God.}}

- [agree] Thomas 113. The disciples ask when the kingdom will come. It will not come by watching for it. It is spread over the earth and people do not see it. (Compare Luke 17:20-21.){{fn:Luke 17:20-21. Qur’an 7:187: the Hour comes upon you suddenly.}}
Sayings that conflict with the Qur’an, and sayings that only repeat another, are listed with the reason for each on the page of sayings set aside.
26: The Gospel of Thomas has no account of an arrest, a trial or a crucifixion, so it neither confirms nor contradicts Qur’an 4:157.
Sayings of Thomas that are not used are listed, each with its reason, on the page of sayings set aside.
